jobs.title: Manager, Strategic Initiatives & Business Transformation
jobs.description:
The Manager, GMNS Strategic Programs & Risk sits within Global Governance, Risk, Remediation, and Operations (GRRO), a Center of Excellence for Global Merchant & Network Services (GMNS). GRRO partners across the organization to drive strategic initiatives, enhance operating rigor, and deliver against enterprise priorities.
This role is ideal for someone who thrives in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, enjoys solving complex problems, and can bring structure, clarity, and momentum to cross-functional initiatives.
You will be part of a small, high-impact team that operates at the intersection of strategy, operations, and risk, leading priority initiatives that span multiple teams, markets, and senior stakeholders.
The role is less about owning a single domain and more about acting as a strategic operator, someone who can quickly get up to speed on new problems, define a path forward, and drive execution across a matrixed organization.
You’ll work closely with partners across GMNS, Risk, Compliance, and other functions to:
- Translate complex challenges into clear, actionable plans

- Align stakeholders around a common direction

- Drive execution with discipline and transparency
- 4–7 years of experience in management consulting, strategy, business operations, or program management within a complex, matrixed organization.

- Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive them to execution.

- Strong communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex topics into clear, concise narratives for senior stakeholders.

- Proven experience influencing across teams and levels without direct authority.

- Highly organized with strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, evolving environment with shifting priorities.

- Analytical mindset with the ability to use data to support decision-making.

- Experience working on cross-functional or enterprise-wide initiatives is strongly preferred.

Exposure to risk, compliance, or regulatory environments is helpful, but not required.
- Lead high-priority, cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through execution, bringing structure to ambiguous business challenges.

- Partner with senior stakeholders to shape strategic direction, align on priorities, and drive decision-making across teams.

- Break down complex problems into clear workstreams, timelines, and deliverables, ensuring progress is tracked and communicated effectively.

- Synthesize inputs from multiple sources (data, stakeholder perspectives, regulatory considerations) into clear insights and recommendations.

- Establish and run governance forums, including executive updates, to ensure alignment, visibility, and accountability.

- Identify risks, dependencies, and trade-offs, and proactively work with stakeholders to navigate them.

- Drive collaboration across global teams, adapting approaches to different markets, functions, and operating environments.

- Support the design and implementation of sustainable processes, frameworks, and ways of working.

jobs.title: Campus - Internship Programme - MBA - Enterprise Strategy Manager - 2027 (UK - London)
jobs.description:
About Enterprise Strategy:
Enterprise Strategy is the internal consulting division of American Express. We work directly with the CEO, the executive team, and senior leaders to provide thought leadership and an external perspective on the most important strategic priorities of the company.
How will you make an impact in this role?
- As a Senior Manager Intern, you will be tackling the most important strategic opportunities and challenges facing American Express today. Projects are primarily oriented around growth strategy in order to drive long-term success and innovation for American Express.
- You will own project workstreams end-to-end, including scoping and structuring problems, conducting complex analyses and research, and creating presentations. You’ll collaborate closely with your teammates to develop solutions and present recommendations to senior leaders.
- You will collaborate with cross-functional teams and stakeholders across the enterprise, including C-suite executives, to drive strategic initiatives that enhance the leadership position of American Express. You will establish yourself as a trusted thought partner to your business partners.
- As a member of the Enterprise Strategy team, you’ll join a close-knit and supportive group of colleagues who put an emphasis on diversity of perspective, mentorship, fun, and a balanced lifestyle.
Minimum Qualifications:
- Currently enrolled in a full-time MBA program or equivalent.
- Students must have a graduation date between December 2027 - August 2028.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Strong problem-solving skills and business acumen to advise executive leadership
- Excellent written and verbal communication
- Strong project management skills, including prioritization, work planning, execution discipline
- Proficiency with both qualitative and quantitative data analysis
- Interpersonal skills – ability to collaborate effectively in a team

Depending on factors such as business unit requirements, the nature of the position, cost and applicable laws, American Express may provide visa sponsorship for certain positions.

jobs.title: Manager - Strategic Planning
jobs.description:
The Strategy & Transformation team serves as a critical driver of growth initiatives, business oversight functions, and an incubator for net new business development strategies within the U.S, Small & Medium Enterprises Organization (US SME) in Global Commercial Services (GCS). The Manager – Strategic Planning is responsible for developing and implementing strategies that drive efficiency and effectiveness across the US SME organization, lead enterprise-wide collaboration where necessary, and support our long-term growth plans. This is a critical role in ensuring the US SME organization is well positioned to deliver for our customers and shareholders, and support colleagues. The Manager will partner closely across Enterprise stakeholders including the SME Executive Office, client-facing teams (e.g., Sales, Account Development), Control Management, and Merchant Services, among others, to ensure clients realize the full potential of American Express Card & Non-Card product offerings.
A successful candidate will be a motivated initiative-taker who is passionate about and has experience bringing others along in a fast-paced environment. This role may be a great fit for talent experienced in driving strategic planning and transformation initiatives which span from concept development to Go-To-Market planning, through to designing Key Performance Indicators for measuring success across large organizations.
- 5+ years of professional experience, preferably with exposure to sales organizations, payments, partner management, and/or strategic planning.
- Proven ability to structure ambiguous business problems, lead matrixed initiatives, influence senior stakeholders, and drive alignment with limited direction across cross-functional teams and organizations.
- Strong analytical, financial, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate strategies across growth, customer experience, operational, and risk dimensions.
- Exceptional project management and process design skills, with experience translating strategy into execution plans and measurable outcomes.
- Intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and a collaborative leadership style
- Bachelor’s degree required, MBA a plus

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.
- Drive strategic initiatives that create value, improve operational efficiency, and support US SME growth and risk management priorities.
- Lead cross-functional workstreams across US SME, Sales, Account Development, Control Management, Merchant Services, and other Enterprise partners to align priorities and execute business initiatives while minimizing risk.
- Develop and deliver executive-ready materials, agendas, and internal processes for senior leadership and key stakeholder forums.
- Translate customer and colleague feedback into roadmap priorities, partner plans, and strategic recommendations.
- Build, implement, and monitor plans that deliver measurable outcomes while ensuring adherence to controls, processes, and compliance expectations.

jobs.title: Manager Assistant – Chief of Staff, Merchant Operations
jobs.description:
At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. As part of Team Amex, you'll experience this powerful backing with comprehensive support for your holistic well-being and many opportunities to learn new skills, develop as a leader, and grow your career.
Here, your voice and ideas matter, your work makes an impact, and together, you will help us define the future of American Express.

How will you make an impact in this role?
The Manager’s Assistant (MA) to the VP of Merchant Operations will play a critical role in supporting the VP and Merchant Operations Leadership Team in defining and executing the organization’s strategic agenda. This individual will help establish and manage the operating rhythm of the VP’s office, ensuring the team remains focused on its priorities, measures progress effectively, and delivers against key commitments.

The MA will serve as a trusted thought partner to the VP and a key collaborator across Merchant Operations leadership, GRRO leadership, and partners across the organization. This is a hands-on role requiring strong analytical and operational capabilities, business judgment, executive communication, and organizational discipline. The successful candidate will be proactive, comfortable moving between strategic and administrative priorities, and able to anticipate needs and drive work forward with limited direction.
Merchant Operations is an international organization. The MA will work across markets and time zones and must have the flexibility to participate in meetings and support key priorities outside of traditional local business hours when needed.
- Experience in operations, analytics, MerchantForce , COE, field/client-facing roles, or a similar environment preferred

- Strong business acumen and the ability to connect operational performance, frontline realities, and strategic priorities

- Hands-on experience producing and maintaining accurate business and operational reports; ability to interpret data, uncover trends and performance drivers, and translate findings into actionable business insights

- Strong collaboration and relationship-management skills, with the ability to work effectively with senior leaders and partners across functions and geographies

- Advanced Excel and data-analysis skills; familiarity with reporting, visualization, or analytics tools preferred

- Experience designing and managing KPIs, scorecards, dashboards, and other performance-management frameworks preferred

- Demonstrated proactive mindset, with the ability to anticipate needs, take initiative, solve problems, and drive work forward

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear, compelling executive-level presentations and narratives

- Strong organizational and business-management discipline, with the ability to manage recurring administrative and operational processes, multiple stakeholders, and competing deadlines with accuracy and follow-through

- Ability to serve as a thought partner, bringing an independent perspective, asking thoughtful questions, and connecting strategy with practical execution

- Ability to operate with independence, judgment, discretion, and comfort with ambiguity in a fast-paced environment

- Experience working across international teams and time zones, with flexibility to support an international schedule when required

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.
- Establish and manage the operating rhythm for the VP and Merchant Operations (MO) Leadership Team, including team agendas, business reviews, planning sessions, decision forums, action tracking, and follow-up

- Partner with the VP and Leadership Team to shape and manage the organization’s strategic agenda, translating priorities into clear initiatives, milestones, measures of success, and deliverables

- Support development of and maintain Merchant Operations KPIs, scorecards, dashboards, and other performance-management tools that provide visibility into progress and areas requiring leadership attention

- Own MO operational and performance reporting, including creating and running recurring reports, analyzing results, identifying trends and performance drivers, and translating data into actionable insights

- Track strategic initiatives and commitments, proactively identifying risks, dependencies, and emerging issues and driving appropriate follow-up and escalation

- Own key monthly, quarterly, and annual business management processes, including headcount tracking and reporting, organizational and distribution list maintenance, recurring submissions and deliverables, and support for mid-year and year-end colleague processes

- Support development of senior leadership presentations, business updates, and executive communications that clearly articulate the Merchant Operations strategy, performance, progress, opportunities, and decisions required

- Serve as a thought partner to the VP, synthesizing information, developing perspectives, pressure-testing ideas, and supporting key decisions and leadership discussions

- Collaborate closely with Merchant Operations leadership, GRRO leadership, and cross-functional partners to advance shared priorities, resolve issues, manage dependencies, and drive initiatives to completion

- Support town halls, colleague communications, leadership meetings, and recognition programs, helping connect colleagues to the organization’s strategy and celebrate contributions

- Proactively identify opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen operating routines, improve reporting, and increase the effectiveness of the VP and Leadership Team

- Build strong relationships across an international organization, collaborating effectively across markets, cultures, and time zones

jobs.title: Manager - Program Management - Enterprise Data Platforms
jobs.description:
The Enterprise Technology Services organization partners with every part of the American Express business to power the company’s growth and innovation with trust and efficiency and drive competitive differentiation with speed. We support the delivery and operations of technology, digital, and data capabilities, platforms, and services globally. Specifically, our team is responsible for the Enterprise Bid Data Platform and engineering, architecture, and Platform enablement supporting 20+ Lines of Business across American Express.   Our Big data Platform is  the backbone of enterprise data – driving scalable, secure, and high-performance for the enterprise data warehouse powering data-driven insights across American Express. This role will drive technical delivery across multiple initiatives that support the resilience, innovation, and growth of our big data platform.
Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering) and/or comparable experience; advanced degree preferred
- Knowledge of Agile/SAFe/Lean methodologies
- 8–12+ years in technical program management, delivering large-scale data and platform initiatives
- Proven track record managing cloud-based data platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP) and big data ecosystems
- Experience leading cross-functional programs spanning data engineering, AI/ML, analytics, and platform teams
- Demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale, multi-year transformations
- Experience implementing or supporting enterprise semantic layers and data standardization initiatives
- Understanding of data-as-a-product models and domain-oriented data ownership
- Familiarity with agentic AI use cases (automation, orchestration, decision intelligence)
- Ability to translate business needs into AI-enabled, data-driven solutions
- Knowledge of technical challenges and systems design, with the ability to facilitate technical discussions and drive solutions

Depending on factors such as business unit requirements, the nature of the position, cost and applicable laws, American Express may provide visa sponsorship for certain position.
How will you make an impact in this role?
- Manage the strategic planning, coordination, and execution of technology-focused projects, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and project goals
- Ability to define and execute complex program roadmaps, aligning business and technology strategies
- Drive technical delivery in Agile, SAFe, and hybrid delivery models
- Ability to have strong dependency management across multiple teams and platforms
- Skilled in risk management, issue resolution, and executive-level reporting
- Experience managing vendor/partner ecosystems and platform integrations
- Strong executive presence with the ability to influence senior leadership and stakeholders
- Experience working across business, product, data, and engineering teams
- Ability to communicate complex technical concepts in clear, business-oriented terms

jobs.title: Director, M&A Integration & Separation
jobs.description:
The M&A Integration and Separation team is a part of Corporate Development organization. The team oversees strategically integrating acquired assets and separating parts of the company undergoing divestiture.   This includes designing the integration/separation strategy in collaboration with the BU sponsor and functional experts, securing executive approval and funding, executing against plans in partnership with target company/buyer and having overall accountability for end-to-end program and outcome.
Along with owning corporate integration/separation globally, the team’s responsibilities also include leading efforts to leverage the company’s assets to maximize value, championing opportunities to leverage the acquisitions’ assets to benefit the company’s existing businesses and in some cases partnering with senior leaders to craft the strategy.   The team works closely with the M&A organization, also part of Corporate Development, along with teams across the company to effectively manage integrations/separations.
How will you make an impact in this role?
The Director will mobilize and lead functional and business teams through M&A integration/Separation planning and execution, while also contributing to ongoing development of American Express’ integration/separation infrastructure and process improvements.
On each project, the Director will be the primary liaison with executive sponsors across the business and counterparts within the target company/buyer and will hold overall accountability for each project’s success.   The Director will also ensure that continuous improvement to the M&A integration/separation process is being incorporate after each engagement leveraging lessons learned and industry best practices.
- Demonstrated experience leading M&A integrations within a corporate/in-house environment, with direct accountability for integration planning and execution.
- 3+ years of experience operating at a director-equivalent level, leading complex enterprise, or M&A integration programs across multiple phases of the lifecycle, including pre-close planning, Day 1 readiness, execution, value realization, and transition to business-as-usual.
- Proven experience leading large-scale, complex integrations involving multiple business units, geographies and/or functions, with significant organizational, technology, operational and regulatory dependencies
- Experience leading M&A integrations required; experience with divestitures, separations and/or carve-outs preferred
- Excellent interpersonal and written/verbal communication skills, and influencing abilities
- Strong analytical rigor, complex problem solving and critical thinking abilities
- A self-starter, comfortable operating in ambiguity
- Demonstrated people leadership experience, including coaching, developing and managing high-performing professionals.
*Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the U.S. is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.
- Partner with business groups to understand, outline, and influence business strategy and its implication on integration/separation
- Lead business and functional teams to create strategic approaches to complex projects with effective plans that capture maximum value from each transaction
- Drive project progress by managing cross-functional teams, overcoming obstacles/risks, developing strategic recommendations, and ensuring deliverables are optimally executed
- Establish and lead integration/separation governance, including cross-functional decision-making, executive escalation, milestone management and accountability across workstreams.
- Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team of M&A integration managers, providing direction across integration/separation initiatives and supporting their ongoing professional development.
- Identify and manage critical cross-functional dependencies, translating them into a cohesive integration/separation roadmap
- Develop effective working relationships with key stakeholders to achieve results and enact value identified in deal rationale
- Serve as a trusted advisor to business leaders, framing complex integration decisions, surfacing trade-offs and risks, and driving timely decisions across stakeholders with competing priorities.

jobs.title: Manager - Americas Business Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT ENTERPRISE SHARED SERVICES
Enterprise Shared Services (ESS) comprises key functions that are core to the company’s operations, including Global Real Estate & Workplace Experience, Global Supply Management, Business Resilience & Corporate Functions Governance, Aviation, Internal Fraud, and Global Security. ESS helps keep our company growing and puts our colleagues at the center of everything they do by delivering best-in-class services that power safe, resilient, and efficient operations around the world.
THE OPPORTUNITY
The Business Operations Lead helps leaders turn priorities into action and make informed decisions about performance, investments, and resources. The role brings together program management, financial planning, and business analytics, with the focus flexing based on the needs of the organization. This colleague will create structure around complex work, connect insights across teams, and help ensure key initiatives are delivered with clear ownership, disciplined execution, and measurable outcomes.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
- Experience in business operations, program management, finance, strategy, analytics, or related work that demonstrates comparable skills.

- Demonstrated ability to lead complex work across multiple teams, stakeholders, and competing priorities.

- Strong financial and analytical skills, including the ability to interpret data and explain the business implications.

- Experience developing plans, performance reporting, financial analyses, or decision-support materials for leaders.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex information clear and actionable.

- Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and bring structure to evolving or ambiguous business needs.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Experience supporting a large, global, or highly matrixed organization.

- Experience with annual planning, forecasting, investment governance, portfolio management, or enterprise-wide initiatives.

- Advanced experience with financial modeling, data visualization, reporting, and presentation tools.

- Experience using data to identify performance drivers, develop recommendations, and measure business outcomes.

- Experience preparing materials and recommendations for senior leaders.

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.
- Lead planning and execution for complex, cross-functional initiatives, establishing clear milestones, ownership, dependencies, risks, and outcomes.

- Establish effective operating rhythms and governance that help leaders prioritize work, track progress, resolve issues, and make timely decisions.

- Partner with Finance and business leaders on budgets, forecasts, investment planning, resource allocation, and ongoing financial performance.

- Develop financial analyses and business cases that clarify tradeoffs and support investment and prioritization decisions.

- Define and track meaningful performance measures; build reporting and analyses that highlight trends, risks, opportunities, and business drivers.

- Translate financial, operational, and performance data into clear insights and actionable recommendations for leaders.

- Create concise, executive-ready updates that communicate progress, decisions, risks, and areas requiring attention.

- Build strong partnerships across functions and influence outcomes by connecting strategy, resources, execution, and measurement.

- Identify opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and improve how the organization operates.

jobs.title: Senior Manager - Strategic Planning
jobs.description:
The American Express mission is to be the world’s most respected service brand. Within American Express, Global Servicing (GS) plays a central role in helping the company achieve that vision, with an interconnected team of nearly 30,000 employees and partners operating in 22 markets around the world, all focused on serving our customers and shareholders.
Within Global Servicing (GS), the Global Servicing Strategy & Transformation team (GSST) is responsible for providing strategic and executional support for Global servicing creating, advising and implementing cross business unit strategies that deliver on our key goals of driving operational effectiveness, customer outcomes and revenue for American Express.
Within GSST, the Servicing Engineering & Optimization (SEO) team is responsible for devising and implementing near- and long-term, cross-GS strategies, programs and products that deliver on our key goals of elevating customer servicing experience, improving operational efficiency, and driving revenue for the Blue Box.
- Experience in Project Management, Business Management, or similar background is required
- Creative thinking, including the ability to identify patterns and propose unconventional solutions to long-standing business problems, and ability to act as a catalyst for change
- Must be an outstanding analytical thinker and problem solver, comfortable working with data and able to resolve complex problems independently
- Strong written and verbal communication skills combined with an ability to interact effectively with senior leaders and business partners
- Proven ability to quickly adjust to shifting priorities, multiple demands, ambiguity, and rapid change
- Proven track record of successfully operating in a highly matrix environment and being able to lead and influence without direct authority
- Strong working knowledge of internal Global Services Group processes and functional areas, particularly Customer Engagement Network processes.

Preferred Additional:
·       Project management, Six Sigma Certification
·       Bachelor’s /Master’s Degree in Industrial Engineering, Management Science, similar degree or 3+ years related work experience leading project teams
Reporting to the Director of SEO, the responsibilities of this role include:

- Responsible for conducting structured analysis to inform and build business strategy including identifying and synthesizing opportunity areas and risks backed by data

- Develop and build business structured business cases for steering and executive decisioning and investment framing quantifying financial customer and operational impact and tradeoffs against markets and capabilities
- Drive implementation of large, medium, and small-scale projects that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of GS functions

jobs.title: Director - Small Business Strategy & Go-To-Market
jobs.description:
American Express Global Commercial Services (GCS) is the leading payment issuer and partner for businesses and corporations of all sizes. The Global Commercial Services Marketing team (GCSM) is responsible for making business membership essential by creating and delivering world-class marketing for our differentiated products and services that drives demand and inspires engaged customers across the lifecycle.
Within GCSM, the Strategy, Brand & Transformation (SBT) team helps turn priorities into marketing and capabilities that resonate with business audiences. In close partnership with our Small Business and Corporate marketing teams, SBT shapes our go-to-market and creative approach, builds awareness and demand through brand activation, and advances the tools and technology that make our marketing stronger. Together, we create cohesive user experiences that build our brand and drive business growth. This role will have a dedicated focus on the Small Business segment, shaping how we bring our products, value propositions, and benefits to market and strengthening the relevance and differentiation of American Express for Small Business customers.
This individual will lead holistic marketing and go-to-market strategies for priority Small Business initiatives, including Card product refreshes and new or enhanced partner benefits.
The Director will bring fresh thinking to transform how we go to market—shifting from individual product launches to ongoing, iterative solutions that deepen customer value. They will turn business, customer, and competitive insights into differentiated propositions, compelling narratives, and integrated strategies that drive acquisition, engagement, and loyalty.
Minimum Qualifications:
- Proven experience developing marketing strategy and go-to-market plans for products, propositions, benefits, or other complex customer offerings , ideally within financial services, payments, B2B, or Small Business.
- Strong strategic marketer with demonstrated ability to connect customer needs, product capabilities, competitive dynamics, and business objectives into differentiated value propositions and actionable GTM strategies.
- Demonstrated success transforming go-to-market models—moving beyond one-time launches to build, test, learn, and optimize ongoing customer solutions.

- Strong customer-first orientation and ability to translate product features and partnership benefits into simple, compelling reasons for customers to engage and choose the brand.
- Analytical problem solver who can synthesize customer research, competitive intelligence, performance data, and business inputs into clear insights and recommendations.
- Proven ability to lead through influence and mobilize complex, cross-functional teams without direct authority.
- Exceptional communicator and storyteller across written, verbal, and visual formats, with demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and drive alignment around strategic recommendations.
- Comfortable operating in ambiguous, fast-paced environments with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and high executive visibility.
- Hands-on, proactive, and highly accountable, with the ability to move fluidly between strategic thinking and executional detail.
- Strong relationship builder with demonstrated collaboration, influencing, and negotiation skills across functions and levels.
- People leadership experience, with the ability to coach, motivate, and develop talent while driving high standards of performance.

Preferred Qualifications:
- 8–10 years of business and marketing experience preferred.

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.
- Lead Small Business Marketing Strategy & GTM: Own end-to-end strategy for priority initiatives, from proposition development through launch, optimization, and ongoing engagement. Define the value proposition, positioning, messaging, audience, channel approach, and integrated customer experience—evolving GTM from episodic launches to iterative, always-on solutions.

- Turn Insights into Strategy: Leverage customer research, behavioral and performance data, competitive intelligence, and market trends to identify opportunities and inform product positioning, messaging, creative strategy, and GTM decisions.

- Drive Cross-Functional Alignment: Mobilize and align partners across Marketing, Small Business Product, and Communications, and other key functions to move complex initiatives from strategy through execution.
- Develop Customer-Centric Messaging: Partner with channel and creative teams to translate product features and partner benefits into clear, differentiated, and relevant customer messaging across acquisition and existing customer experiences.
- Create Integrated GTM Roadmaps: Establish clear strategies, milestones, decision points, dependencies, and measurement frameworks to ensure disciplined execution across multiple concurrent initiatives.
- Measure and Optimize Impact: Define success metrics and leverage performance insights to assess GTM effectiveness, identify opportunities for optimization, and inform future product and marketing strategies.
- Influence Senior Leadership: Develop clear, compelling, and visually engaging narratives that articulate strategic choices, recommendations, progress, risks, and business impact to senior leaders.
Director, Marketing Strategy and Go-to-Market
